key_insight: A mixed quantum energy estimator uses sparse multiconfiguration references to sharply reduce the measurements needed for correlated energy differences in a challenging photodynamic-material model.
engineering_relevance: Lower sampling costs and simpler target-state preparation could make quantum chemistry calculations for therapy-relevant materials more practical.
method: Combine a quantum-prepared target state with sparse multiconfiguration reference states.
Recover ground-state energy corrections using magnitude-only compute-uncompute measurements.
Integrate AI-assisted state preparation and error detection in a 50-qubit demonstration.
evidence_signal: Analytical variance estimates predict 1.6 mHa precision with a few hundred shots—about 100× fewer than a single-determinant formulation and 1,000× fewer than optimized Hamiltonian-term sampling—with emulator and Quantinuum Helios validation up to a (10,10) active space.
watch_item: The sampling advantages are analytically predicted; broader practical gains require accounting for reference construction, state preparation, and error-detection overhead.
paper_title: Measurement-efficient energy estimator for quantum chemistry of photodynamic materials
